extracted.intended_audience: prospective and current students of The Second City Training Center (comedy/improv)
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of class selection, enrollment policies, prerequisites, progression, and student rules for The Second City Training Center. Guidance aimed at helping new and continuing students choose classes, understand requirements (auditions, age, credit), and navigate payment/attendance/return policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to begin / program selection
rubrics_metrics.description: It depends what you’d like to do. The Improvisation Program is a great jumping off point. We also have Improv for Anxiety, Public Speaking and Acting as great first options. Or if you’re looking to go the writing route, we have the Writing or Stand Up Programs. If you have completed a full year of improv training (equivalent to our Improv Program) from another training centre and you have completed a post secondary acting course, then you are eligible to submit for our Conservatory Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need help deciding which classes to take, call the office; staff will discuss your interests and goals and recommend where to begin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference between Acting and Improv classes
rubrics_metrics.description: While both of these core programs use similar improvisational techniques derived from the teachings of Viola Spolin, the focus for the performer is different. In the Improv program, we teach you how to work, play & perform without a script. In the Acting program, we show you how to use those improv skills to be a better, more present actor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Later levels of the Acting program also incorporate scripts and memorized text including scenes from the Second City Archives; choose Acting to develop scripted performance skills and Improv to focus on unscripted performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audition requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Only some advanced programs like the Sketch Conservatory require auditions, though some specialized classes and workshops may have prerequisites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assume most beginner/regular classes do not require auditions; check specific advanced programs for audition or prerequisite requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic credit and visa support
rubrics_metrics.description: Because the Training Centre itself is not an accredited institution of higher learning, students are generally ineligible for college credit. We also cannot file the paperwork for international students to obtain student visas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An exception: the Comedy Studies program run in Chicago in partnership with Columbia College is an accredited college program for which students receive college credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: We offer classes in our Kids and Teens Program for students ages 4-18. Students must be at least 19 to attend classes in our adult programs or at least a high school graduate, but there is no upper age limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify program-specific age rules (kids/teens vs adult) before enrolling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment timing and accepted methods
rubrics_metrics.description: We require payment at the time of registration in order to hold your spot in the class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted payment methods: Mastercard, Visa, Amex, cash, or cheque. Payment plans are available — register online and set up a payment plan or inquire with the office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tuition refund and transfer policy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have a schedule conflict, contact Customer Service as soon as possible to see if arrangements can be made. Transfers may be subject to a $25 transfer fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarships availability
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page links to more information — contact the Training Centre or follow the scholarships link for eligibility and application details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class section naming convention
rubrics_metrics.description: We have lots of classes, and sometimes we have multiple sections of the same class running at the same time. In those cases we add various words to the class names so you know which class you belong to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are continuing to the next level of a program on the same day and time, enroll in the same word group to ensure you register for the correct section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence & makeup policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have to miss a class, please reach out to our Customer Service team for options. We do not offer scheduled makeup classes but will assist you as best we can.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact your instructor for any material you may have missed. Try to get to every class so you don’t miss content and can advance to the next level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave of absence and reentry policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Sometimes a student may wish or need to take time off from The Training Centre due to personal reasons. Should this occur, please contact The Training Centre staff immediately. Please be informed that when you return, the Training Centre will place you at its discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students who leave during the Conservatory Program may be asked to re-audition. Returning students must pay the tuition rate applicable at time of rejoining. Any student returning after more than one (1) year of absence is required to rejoin the program at a level determined by The Training Centre.

rubrics_metrics.name: No guarantee of employment with Second City
rubrics_metrics.description: It takes a great deal of training and experience to become a member of our professional company. Most of the resident actors have trained and performed for a number of years before being hired by The Second City.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although many resident company actors are graduates of the Training Centre, completion of any program does not guarantee employment with the company.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended pathway for aspiring performers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Conservatory is our cornerstone training program designed to give you first-hand experience in the Second City method. It caters to the aspiring professional, and it qualifies you to audition for our house teams and other advanced programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admission to the Conservatory is by audition and requires some previous experience — you may need to start with training in the Improvisation program. Complementary classes (Acting, Comedy Writing, music/singing) help develop scripted performance, writing, and musical skills; students may take these before or after the Conservatory to round out skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jams, open mics, workshops, and special events access
rubrics_metrics.description: Jams + Open Mics: The one-stop-shop for all student jams, open mics, workshops, and special events! Come to play or to watch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Events are recommended for current students only; see the schedule for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Center wishlist / feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: The Training Center Wishlist: Not seeing what you hoped? Submit your suggestions here for classes, Training Center events, jams, workshops, etc. you’d like to see offered in the future.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Training Centre welcomes student feedback and suggestions for future offerings.
